papers.title: Open-World Scientific Discovery
papers.current_ceiling: The bounded methods/system-design paper is ready; TREC-COVID superiority failed its registered joint gate.
post_matrix_updates: Canonical manuscript PDF exists, but the journal package remains superseded and must be rebuilt separately from new science.
load_bearing_adverse: TREC-COVID recall@100 difference is -0.0177 with bootstrap interval [-0.0273,-0.0091], breaching the -0.02 noninferiority lower bound.
Read cost is 2.8× where the gate required at least 25% fewer reads.
nDCG@10 improved by +0.1488, but a secondary metric outside the gate cannot rescue the failed recall/cost terminal.
papers.strongest_remaining_gap: A new, disjoint BEIR study must test whether the open-world pipeline improves discovery utility under a prospectively joint effectiveness-and-cost criterion, not repeat TREC-COVID.
papers.decisive_question: On frozen SciFact, NFCorpus and ArguAna tasks, can the unchanged open-world pipeline match the strongest donor product on recall while reducing total evidence-access cost and controlling false novelty?
papers.maximum_claim_if_supported: The pipeline is a useful open-world discovery architecture when evaluated on a joint retrieval, cost and claim-validity frontier across independent task families.
papers.hypothesis_or_theorem: The same frozen policy should satisfy a noninferiority gate on coverage/recall, an improvement gate on full resource cost and a noncompensatory false-novelty bound across the three E11 datasets.
papers.population_or_universe: All eligible E11 topics/documents under pinned versions; TREC-COVID and all previously accessed topics are excluded from confirmation.
papers.unit_of_analysis: Topic × system arm, with claim-level verification nested within topics where applicable.
historical_only_inputs: TREC-COVID and all old P2 outcomes
design: Freeze exact BEIR versions, topic eligibility and document corpora.
Implement donor-complete lexical, dense and hybrid retrieval comparators under matched access.
Keep policy unchanged across datasets except prospectively allowed corpus adapters.
Separate retrieval endpoints from downstream claim/novelty verification.
Account for reads, tokens, model calls, latency and cache.
primary_endpoints: Recall@100 or dataset-native coverage as the primary effectiveness endpoint.
Total evidence reads/tool calls and latency.
nDCG@10 as a secondary endpoint that cannot rescue a failed primary gate.
analysis_plan: Paired topic bootstrap with dataset-level hierarchical synthesis.
Joint gate and decision order frozen before execution.
Multiplicity controlled across three datasets and co-primary endpoints.
Missing topics/runs are retained under a frozen worst-case or CANNOT_CHECK rule.
papers.power_or_exhaustion_rule: Use every official eligible topic; if claim-level adjudication is sampled, power it prospectively and stratify by dataset before any system output is opened.
papers.success_gate: Recall/coverage is noninferior, full resource cost improves under the frozen gate, false novelty does not worsen and at least two datasets independently support the joint terminal.
papers.refutation_gate: Failure of any co-primary gate preserves the bounded architecture paper but does not support superiority; nDCG alone cannot rescue.
papers.cannot_check_gate: CANNOT_CHECK if dataset versions, access matching, donor implementations or claim-verification authority are incomplete.
papers.authority_required: Official relevance judgments plus independent claim adjudication where retrieval gold does not decide scientific support.

active_lane.collision_rule: TREC-COVID is historical only; the new identity must not modify the failed P2 terminal.

immediate_safe_actions: Rebuild the current journal package and claim-to-PDF audit independently of the successor.
Write the E11 donor-product implementation matrix.
Freeze a false-novelty adjudication protocol before system outputs.
forbidden_actions: Do not reuse TREC-COVID for fresh confirmation.
Do not let nDCG rescue failed recall/cost.
Do not compare against BM25 alone when a stronger donor product is feasible.
papers.journal_bar: A top-tier IR/discovery paper needs strong modern baselines, multi-dataset evidence, joint quality/cost gates, false-novelty authority and full negative-history reporting.
papers.sibling_boundary: Owns open-world discovery/retrieval; scientific promotion governance belongs to ORION-14/24.
